mainTopic: What מחיצה means in the opening משנה of בבא בתרא, and whether היזק ראיה (harm from being seen) counts as damage.
overview: The opening משנה says that partners who 'wanted to make a מחיצה' in a shared courtyard build a wall in the middle. The גמרא first finishes a proof that מחיצה means a partition-wall. On that reading, the wall is built only when both partners agree, so היזק ראיה (harm from being seen) is not called damage. The גמרא then suggests that מחיצה means 'division,' which would point the other way. It goes back to the partition reading by looking closely at the משנה's wording. Next it explains why the משנה needs to say the wall goes 'in the middle': it covers a partner who was talked into building. Then the גמרא challenges the idea that היזק ראיה is not damage, using a list of sources: the garden, a fallen wall, a gatehouse, dividing a courtyard, windows, and רב נחמן's rule about a roof. Each proof is pushed aside by showing that its case is different. The answer to the last proof, the roof, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the proof from a vineyard wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about a broken vineyard wall. It is being used as proof that the word מחיצה means a physical partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the vineyard owner gave up on the broken wall and did not fix it, he has made the crops forbidden as כלאים, and he must pay for the loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from another משנה about a vineyard whose wall (מחיצה) broke down. This quote proves that the word מחיצה can mean a physical partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, מחיצה clearly means an actual wall between the vineyard and the grain field. If the owner neglects it, the grain becomes forbidden as כלאים and he must pay. So the word מחיצה is used there for a physical barrier (גודא).

keyTerms.meaning: gave up on, stopped caring about
made forbidden (as כלאים in a vineyard)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not from our משנה about the courtyard. It is the end of a quote from a different משנה about a vineyard, which the גמרא brings as proof for the meaning of the word מחיצה.

phrases.english: If he gave up on it and did not fence it,
he has made the crops forbidden,
phrases.notes: Literally 'made holy.' Here it means the grain and grapes became forbidden as כלאים.

phrases.english: and he is responsible for the loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה that began before this section, proving that מחיצה means a partition.
steps.raayaObject: That the word מחיצה in our משנה means a physical partition (גודא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a vineyard wall (מחיצת הכרם) that broke and was not repaired.

steps.title: Conclusion: harm from being seen is not damage
steps.stepSummary: If מחיצה means a partition, the wall is built only because both partners wanted it. So a partner who does not want a wall cannot be forced to build one, which shows that היזק ראיה is not called damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason they build is that they both wanted to. If they did not want to, we do not force him. So harm from being seen is not called damage.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the reading that מחיצה means a partition, the גמרא draws a legal conclusion from the wording 'שרצו' (they wanted). Since the wall is built only when both partners agree, היזק ראיה is not considered damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says 'partners who wanted to make a מחיצה build a wall.' If the wall itself is what they 'wanted,' then without agreement there is no wall. If seeing into your neighbor's space counted as damage, we would force a wall even without agreement. Since we do not, היזק ראיה is not called damage.

keyTerms.meaning: harm from being seen, loss of privacy

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether היזק ראיה counts as real damage is the big question running through this sugya, and the meaning of one word in the משנה decides it here.

phrases.english: The reason is that they wanted,
phrases.notes: This refers back to our משנה: 'partners who wanted to make a מחיצה.'

phrases.english: but if they did not want,
we do not obligate him;
apparently, harm from being seen
is not called damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the proven meaning (מחיצה is a partition) and draws a halachic inference about היזק ראיה.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה is not called damage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'שרצו' in our משנה, read with מחיצה meaning a partition.

steps.title: Maybe מחיצה means division
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that מחיצה might mean 'division,' as in the פסוק 'מחצת העדה.' Then 'wanting' refers only to dividing the courtyard, and the wall is forced on the unwilling partner, which would show that היזק ראיה is damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that מחיצה means division, as it is written 'and the half of the congregation was.' Then, once they wanted to divide, we build the wall even against his will, so harm from being seen is called damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first reading by offering a different meaning of the word מחיצה, which would flip the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מחיצה means 'division,' then the partners only agreed to split the courtyard. The wall is then something the court forces on the unwilling partner. The only reason to force a wall would be to protect privacy, so היזק ראיה would be called damage.

keyTerms.meaning: half of, the divided portion of

phrases.english: But say 'מחיצה' means a division,
as it is written: 'And the half of the congregation was';
and since they wanted to divide,
they build the wall even against his will,
so apparently harm from being seen is called damage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 2 by offering a different meaning of the key word.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that היזק ראיה is not called damage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof depends on מחיצה meaning a partition. If it means 'division,' the wall is forced against one partner's will, which shows that היזק ראיה is damage.

steps.title: The wording 'make a מחיצה' does not fit 'division'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'division' reading. If that were the meaning, the משנה should have used the simple verb 'לחצות' (to divide) instead of 'לעשות מחיצה' (to make a מחיצה).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'who wanted to make a מחיצה'? It should have said 'who wanted to divide'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 3 by looking closely at the משנה's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You 'make' a physical thing like a wall. If the משנה only meant 'divide,' it would have used the plain verb 'לחצות.' The phrase 'לעשות מחיצה' sounds like building a partition, so the 'division' reading is weakened.

phrases.english: If so,
what is this wording 'who wanted to make a מחיצה'?!
It should have said 'who wanted to divide'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַאי שֶׁרָצוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative reading proposed in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that מחיצה in our משנה means 'division.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'לעשות מחיצה' does not fit 'division'; the plain verb 'לחצות' would have been used.

steps.title: But 'the wall' does not fit 'partition' either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same kind of wording question against the partition reading. If מחיצה already means the wall, the משנה should have said 'they build it,' not 'they build the wall.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does it mean, a partition-wall? Then why say 'they build the wall'? It should have said 'they build it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the partition reading with a wording problem of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מחיצה is the wall, then 'the wall' in the second half of the משנה is the same thing already mentioned. Normally you would just say 'אותו' (it). Repeating the noun suggests the wall is something new, which fits the 'division' reading better.

phrases.english: Rather, what does it mean, a partition-wall?
Then why 'they build the wall'?!
It should have said 'they build it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 favored the partition reading, this step raises a wording difficulty against that reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that מחיצה means a partition-wall (גודא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מחיצה is the wall itself, repeating 'את הכותל' is extra; the משנה should simply have said 'אותו.'

steps.title: 'The wall' teaches that a real wall is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'כותל' was used on purpose. Saying only 'it' might suggest a flimsy fence of pegs is enough, so the משנה tells us a real wall is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had it said 'it,' I would have thought a mere fence of pegs is enough. It teaches us: a real wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the partition reading by explaining why the משנה said 'the wall' instead of 'it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחיצה is a general word for any partition, even a weak one. By saying 'כותל,' the משנה tells us what kind of partition is required: a solid wall, not a fence of pegs. So the extra word adds new information, and the partition reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a flimsy fence made of pegs or stakes

steps.whatToRemember: Reading מחיצה as a partition fits 'לעשות מחיצה,' and 'את הכותל' is explained as requiring a real wall, not a flimsy fence. On this reading, the wall is built only when both partners agree, which suggests that היזק ראיה is not called damage.

phrases.english: Had it taught 'it,'
I would have thought a mere fence of pegs is enough,
so it teaches us: a real wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the seemingly extra word adds new information.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'אותו,' one might think a flimsy fence of pegs is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כותל' teaches that a real wall is required, so the partition reading of מחיצה stands.

steps.title: Why say the wall goes in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, 'they build the wall in the middle,' and asks why this needs saying, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'They build the wall in the middle, etc.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and asks why it bothers to say the wall goes in the middle. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both partners own the courtyard equally, so of course each should give up an equal strip of ground for the wall. The גמרא wants to know what new rule the משנה is teaching with these words.

keyTerms.meaning: etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: They build the wall in the middle, etc.
It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about what מחיצה means and turns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'בונין את הכותל באמצע'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Equal partners obviously split the cost and the ground equally, so the clause seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The partner who was talked into it
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a case where one partner talked the other into building a partition. Without the משנה, we might think the second partner could say he agreed only to a thin divider, not to giving up usable ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed where one partner went first and convinced the other. You might have thought the second one can say: 'When I agreed with you, it was only about the airspace. I never agreed to give up ground I use.' The משנה teaches us that he cannot say this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a partner who was talked into building. It teaches that once he agreed, he must give up his half of the ground for a real wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partner who was talked into it might claim his agreement was small: just a thin divider that blocks the view and takes no real floor space. The משנה rules that agreeing to a partition means agreeing to a proper wall in the middle, with each partner giving up ground equally.

keyTerms.meaning: no, it is needed for a special case
you might have thought... so it teaches us otherwise

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where one went first and convinced his fellow partner;
you might have said that he can say to him:
When I agreed with you, it was about the airspace,
phrases.notes: He means: I agreed to a thin divider that only blocks the air and view between us.

phrases.english: but about the use of the ground, I did not agree with you;
so it teaches us that he cannot say this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא צריכא דקדים חד ורצייה לחבריה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question by pointing to a case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the rule in a specific case where it adds something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A partner who was talked into it could say he agreed only to a thin divider that takes up no usable ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: Agreeing to a partition means each partner gives up equal ground for a proper wall in the middle.

steps.title: Is damage from seeing really not damage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the conclusion of the earlier steps, that היזק ראיה is not called damage, and challenges it. It gives a memory sign listing the challenges that will follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is damage from seeing really not called damage?! (Memory sign: garden, wall, compel, and divide, windows, of רב נחמן.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier conclusion that היזק ראיה is not real damage. It lists, as a memory aid, the sources it will bring to challenge that conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2-6 ended with מחיצה meaning a wall, which showed that an unwilling partner cannot be forced to build, so היזק ראיה is not damage. Now the גמרא asks whether that can really be true, and gets ready to bring several sources that seem to say it is damage.

keyTerms.meaning: damage from being seen; loss of privacy
a memory sign listing the coming discussions

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן is not part of the argument. It is just a list of key words to help remember the challenges that come next.

phrases.english: And is damage from seeing not called damage?!
(Memory sign: garden, wall, compel,
phrases.notes: Each word is a reminder of one challenge the גמרא is about to bring, in order.

phrases.english: and divide, windows, of רב נחמן.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wall-in-the-middle question and returns to the conclusion of steps 2-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that היזק ראיה is not called damage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Several sources seem to treat loss of privacy as real damage, so the conclusion is questioned.

steps.title: The first challenge: the garden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's rule about a garden, where a partner can be forced to help build a partition. This suggests that היזק ראיה is damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And so too in a garden'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first source, from our own משנה, that seems to show היזק ראיה is real damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that in a garden, where the custom is to put up a partition, an unwilling partner is forced to help. The only reason to force him seems to be to protect privacy, which would mean היזק ראיה counts as damage, against the earlier conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; here comes a source

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And so too in a garden'!
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה: in a garden, where the custom is to divide, the unwilling partner is forced to help build.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first item in the memory sign (גינה) to back up the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה is called damage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule 'וכן בגינה': in a garden, an unwilling partner is forced to help build a partition where that is the custom.

steps.title: A garden is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the garden is pushed away. A garden has its own reason for a partition: looking at a growing crop can harm it, as רבי אבא taught in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garden is different. This follows רבי אבא, who said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: a person may not stand in his friend's field while its grain is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 10. It says the garden rule does not show that היזק ראיה is damage, because a garden has a special reason of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a garden, staring at the growing crop can actually harm the plants through an evil eye. That is harm to the crop itself, not just a loss of privacy. So the garden rule tells us nothing about ordinary היזק ראיה in a courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain, crops still growing in the field

phrases.english: A garden is different,
in line with Rabbi Abba,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
It is forbidden for a person to stand in his friend's field
while it is standing with its grain.
phrases.notes: The idea is that staring at someone's growing crop can harm it with an evil eye, so a garden needs protection for its own reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the garden proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the garden; the general question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The garden rule rests on a separate reason: looking at a growing crop harms it. It is not based on privacy damage.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'and similarly'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה links the garden to the courtyard with the word 'and similarly,' so they should share the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'and similarly'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 11. The משנה says 'and similarly in a garden,' which sounds as if the garden works just like the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the garden rule had a different reason, the evil eye, why would the משנה say 'and similarly'? That word suggests the garden and the courtyard follow the same logic, which would bring back the proof about היזק ראיה.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, a word that links two cases

phrases.english: But it teaches "and similarly"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 11 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the garden has a separate reason (step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'And similarly' links the garden to the courtyard, so both should share one reason.

steps.title: 'Similarly' refers only to the building stones
steps.stepSummary: 'And similarly' only means that the garden partition is built with the same kind of stones as the courtyard wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to unhewn and hewn stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word 'similarly' links the garden to the courtyard only in how the wall is built, not in why it is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard section of the משנה described building with rough or cut stones according to local custom. 'And similarly' copies that building detail to the garden. The reason for the garden wall can still be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Rough stones that are not cut or shaped

phrases.english: It is about unhewn and hewn stones.
phrases.notes: The 'similarly' only covers what the wall is made of, following local custom, not why it must be built.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what a word refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And similarly' means the garden shares the courtyard's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'And similarly' only shares the building materials, so the garden can still have its own reason.
steps.whatToRemember: The garden proof falls away. The garden has its own reason (harm to crops), and 'and similarly' only refers to the type of stones.

steps.title: Proof from a courtyard wall that fell
steps.stepSummary: A new proof: when a courtyard wall falls, a partner can be forced to rebuild it up to four אמות. That suggests היזק ראיה is damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a courtyard wall that fell, we obligate him to build it up to four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof against the idea that היזק ראיה is not damage. It quotes a later משנה about a fallen courtyard wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a partner can be forced to rebuild a dividing wall, the only point of that wall is privacy. So privacy damage must count as real damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, the opening of a proof
Four cubits, a height of about 2 meters

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A courtyard wall that fell,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a משנה a little later in the פרק.

phrases.aramaic: מְחַיְּיבִין אוֹתוֹ לִבְנוֹת עַד אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת!
phrases.english: we obligate him to build it up to four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the garden proof fails, the גמרא brings the next challenge listed in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה is called damage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a courtyard wall that fell, where a partner must help rebuild it up to four אמות.

steps.title: A fallen wall is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Where a wall already stood, the partners had already agreed to have one, so they must rebuild it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wall that fell is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 14 with one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partner is forced to rebuild because a wall was already there, and they had once agreed to it. That says nothing about forcing someone to build a brand-new wall because of היזק ראיה.

phrases.english: A wall that fell is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the fallen wall.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a wall that already existed, so the duty to rebuild comes from the earlier agreement, not from privacy damage.

steps.title: Why would anyone bring that proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. The משנה clearly talks about a wall that fell, so why did the questioner think it was a proof?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why the proof in step 14 was brought at all, since the answer 'a fallen wall is different' seems so obvious. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that fell' are right there in the משנה. So the questioner must have had a reason to think they did not matter. The גמרא wants to know that reason.

phrases.english: And the one who raised it,
why did he raise it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the proof that was just rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the questioner was thinking when he brought a case that clearly mentions a fallen wall.

steps.title: The fallen wall was mentioned for the last part of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The questioner thought the משנה spoke of a fallen wall only so it could teach its last part: no one has to build higher than four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needed that case for the last part: above four אמות, we do not obligate him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the questioner's thinking. In his view, 'that fell' is not the reason for the obligation. It is there so the משנה can teach its ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner held that a partner must build a wall even where none stood before. The משנה chose a fallen-wall case to teach a new point: even if the old wall was taller, he only has to rebuild up to four אמות, which is enough to stop the privacy damage.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה

phrases.english: It needed it for the last part:
phrases.notes: He means the fallen wall is mentioned only to teach the ending, not because a wall must have stood there before.

phrases.english: from four cubits and higher
we do not obligate him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The questioner read the fallen-wall case as chosen to teach the ending: no obligation to build above four אמות, even if the old wall was higher.
steps.whatToRemember: The questioner thought partners must build a wall even where none stood before, and that the משנה mentions a fallen wall only to teach the four-אמות limit.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not prove that היזק ראיה is damage. It only explains why the questioner thought his proof worked. The rejection 'a fallen wall is different' still stands.

steps.title: Proof from building a gatehouse and door for the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The residents of a courtyard can force each other to build a gatehouse and a door. So היזק ראיה must count as damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: We force him to build a gatehouse and a door for the courtyard. Learn from this that damage from being seen is called damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from a משנה. Residents of a shared courtyard can force each other to pay for a gatehouse and a door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would people need a gate and a door? So that passersby can't look into the courtyard. If we can force someone to pay to stop people from looking, then being seen must count as real damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
Gatehouse: a small guard room at the courtyard entrance
Damage caused by being seen (loss of privacy)
Learn from it: the proof's conclusion

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We force him to build
phrases.notes: "Him" means each person who lives in the shared courtyard. The others can make him chip in.

phrases.english: a gatehouse and a door for the courtyard.
Learn from it:
damage from being seen is called damage!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ לִבְנוֹת בֵּית שַׁעַר וְדֶלֶת לֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier proof from the fallen courtyard wall was rejected, so the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה is considered real damage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that courtyard residents can force each other to build a gatehouse and door

steps.title: Being seen by the public is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Being exposed to the whole public is worse damage. It tells us nothing about one neighbor seeing another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Damage caused by the public is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the gatehouse proof. That case is about the whole public looking in, not one neighbor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gate and door block the many people walking in the street. Being exposed to crowds is clearly damage. But our question is about one neighbor seeing another, and that may be less serious.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage caused by the public (many people)

phrases.english: Damage from the public is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 18 by pointing out that its case is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not say that היזק ראיה is not damage.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof's case is about the public looking in. Our question is about one neighbor.

steps.title: Proof from dividing a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: isn't one person seeing also damage? It brings the משנה about splitting a courtyard and suggests the split must be a real wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by an individual, is it not damage? Come and hear: We don't divide a courtyard unless there are four אמות for this one and four אמות for that one. This means: if there is enough for this one and enough for that one, we divide. Isn't that with a wall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer and asks whether one person seeing is really not damage. Then it brings a proof from the משנה about dividing a shared courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard is big enough, one partner can demand that it be split. The גמרא suggests this split must be a solid wall. If so, the partner is being forced to block his neighbor's view. That would show that one neighbor seeing another is damage.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual (one person, as opposed to the public)
Four cubits: the minimum useful space for each partner
What, is it not...? (the גמרא suggesting how to read the source)

phrases.english: And by an individual, is it not damage?
Come and hear:
We do not divide the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָזֶה
phrases.english: unless it has four אמות for this one
and four אמות for that one.

phrases.aramaic: הָא יֵשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי לָזֶה וּכְדֵי לָזֶה – חוֹלְקִין;
phrases.english: So if there is enough for this one and enough for that one, we divide;
Isn't that with a wall?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְיָחִיד לָא? תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין חוֹלְקִין אֶת הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19's idea that only public viewing counts. It brings a proof that one person's viewing also counts.
steps.raayaObject: That even one neighbor seeing another is real damage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a courtyard big enough for four אמות each is divided

steps.title: Maybe the division is just a see-through fence
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The division might be a simple fence of pegs that you can still see through.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is with a mere fence of pegs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the courtyard-division proof. The split might only mark the border, not block the view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the split being a solid wall. If it is just a low row of pegs, each partner can still see the other. So nothing is being done to stop the seeing, and there is no proof about היזק ראיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A light fence of pegs that marks a border but can be seen through

phrases.english: No, with a mere fence of pegs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 20 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that the משנה requires a wall.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a solid wall. The משנה may only require a see-through divider.

steps.title: Proof from keeping a wall away from a neighbor's windows
steps.stepSummary: A wall must be kept four אמות from a neighbor's windows. A ברייתא explains that one reason is so no one can peek in. So היזק ראיה is damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Windows, whether above, below, or opposite, need four אמות. And a ברייתא teaches about this: above, so he can't peek and see; below, so he can't stand and see; opposite, so he won't darken the house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof. It cites the משנה about building a wall near a neighbor's windows, plus a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says two of the three distances exist to stop someone from looking into the window. That means the law protects people from being seen. So it seems היזק ראיה is real damage.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא was taught about it (explaining the משנה)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The windows: whether above,
phrases.notes: This is about someone building a wall near his neighbor's windows.

phrases.english: whether below, or whether opposite them,
four אמות.
And it was taught about it:
Above: so that he can't peek in and see;
below: so that he can't stand on it and see;
opposite: so that he won't darken the house!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַחַלּוֹנוֹת, בֵּין מִלְּמַעְלָה בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּה וּבֵין מִכְּנֶגְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the courtyard-division proof failed, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה is real damage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about windows and the ברייתא explaining its distances

steps.title: Being seen inside a house is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Being seen inside your house is worse than being seen in a courtyard. So this proves nothing about a shared courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Damage in a house is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the window proof. Looking into someone's house is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do private things inside their homes, so being seen there is clearly damage. A courtyard is more open, and people may not mind being seen there. So the question of היזק ראיה in a courtyard is still not settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage of being seen inside a house

steps.whatToRemember: Three proofs were pushed aside here: the public (gatehouse), the peg fence (dividing the courtyard), and the house (windows). Each time the גמרא defends the earlier conclusion that ordinary היזק ראיה between neighbors in a courtyard is not damage, by showing that the proof's case is different or can be read another way. The next step brings another proof, from a roof next to a courtyard.

phrases.english: Damage in a house is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 22 by showing that a house is a special case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. A house is more private than a courtyard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The window case is about a house. Our question is about a shared courtyard.

steps.title: Proof from a roof next to a neighbor's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a roof next to a neighbor's courtyard needs a railing four אמות high. This looks like proof that being seen in a courtyard is real damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If a roof is next to a neighbor's courtyard, the roof owner must build a railing four אמות high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof that היזק ראיה is real damage. This time it brings a case of a roof that looks down into a neighbor's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last proof, the windows in Step 22, was pushed away in Step 23 because a house is more private than a courtyard. This new case is about a courtyard, so that answer will not work here. Why else would the roof owner need such a tall railing, if not to stop him from seeing into the courtyard?

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
Roof (flat roofs were used as living space)
A railing or low wall around a roof
Four אמות, about 2 meters, taller than a person

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the regular מעקה for safety, which only needs to be ten טפחים high. A railing of four אמות is much taller than a person, so it is clearly about blocking the view, not about stopping falls.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
A roof that is next to his neighbor's courtyard,
they make for it a railing
phrases.notes: The roof owner is the one who must build it, so he cannot look down into the courtyard.

phrases.english: four אמות high!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the house proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a proof that is about a courtyard, so the house-versus-courtyard answer cannot work.
steps.raayaObject: That היזק ראיה counts as real damage even in a courtyard.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a roof next to a neighbor's courtyard needs a railing four אמות high.

steps.title: A roof is different because its use is not regular
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The courtyard owner uses his courtyard all the time, but the roof owner goes up only now and then. So the courtyard owner never knows when he will be seen. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the courtyard owner can say to the roof owner: I use my courtyard regularly, but you do not use your roof regularly, and I do not know at what time you will go up and come...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts rejecting the roof proof by showing what makes a roof special. The sentence is not finished here; the גמרא completes the reason on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard owner is always in his courtyard, so he can never plan around the roof owner. The roof owner pops up at random times, so the courtyard owner cannot know when to be careful. This special surprise problem may be why a railing is needed, and it tells us nothing about two neighbors sharing a courtyard who see each other normally.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: the case in the proof is special
Use (how often and how one uses a place)

phrases.english: It is different there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ בַּעַל הֶחָצֵר לְבַעַל הַגָּג:
phrases.english: because the owner of the courtyard can say to the owner of the roof:
For me, my use is regular,
for you, your use is not regular;
and I do not know at what time
you go up and come –

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ בַּעַל הֶחָצֵר לְבַעַל הַגָּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the roof proof of Step 24 by pointing to something special about a roof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the roof proof is rejected; the question of היזק ראיה in a shared courtyard stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The roof case has an extra problem, surprise viewing at unknown times, so it cannot prove that ordinary seeing between courtyard neighbors is damage.
